disclaimer: Research, not legal advice. Each fact carries sourceUrl and lastVerified; null means not yet verified. Confirm with the consulate before filing.
name: Spain

visas.name: Non-Lucrative Residence Visa (residencia temporal no lucrativa)

income.basis: 400% of IPREM per month for the applicant (IPREM 2026 = EUR 600/month, EUR 7,200/year)
income.perDependent: +100% of IPREM per family member: EUR 600/month (EUR 7,200/year)
income.note: Rule (400% IPREM applicant, 100% IPREM per family member) from Ministerio de Inclusión Hoja 6 (updated May 2025, cites RD 1155/2024 arts. 60-63) and US consulate pages (Boston, Chicago, Washington). IPREM 2026 = EUR 600/month, EUR 7,200/year (12 pagas): SEPE https://www.sepe.es/HomeSepe/prestaciones-desempleo/Cuantias-anuales.html and Consulate LA https://www.exteriores.gob.es/Consulados/losangeles/en/ServiciosConsulares/Documents/IPREM.pdf; legal basis Ley 31/2022 (PGE 2023) prorogued, IPREM unchanged since 2023. Arithmetic: 4 x 600 = 2,400/month; 2,400 x 12 = 28,800/year. Couple: 2,400 + 600 = 3,000/month (36,000/year). Couple + 1 child: 3,600/month (43,200/year). Washington consulate states the requirement on an annual basis (400% IPREM annually).

savings.basis: Funds covering the first year: 400% IPREM x 12 months (EUR 2,400 x 12); +EUR 7,200 per family member
savings.note: Consulates accept either sufficient own funds for the initial year or a regular income (Chicago, Washington pages). Hoja 6 says means can be proven by any means, including property titles, certified cheques or credit cards with bank certification. The amount is computed from the IPREM rule (4 x 600 x 12), not a figure printed on the page. Chicago also asks for bank account details incl. balances at 31 Dec of the previous year and average balance.

processingTimeDays.note: Boston consulate: legal period for a decision is 3 months from the day after submission, extendable if an interview or extra documents are requested. Inside that, the Oficina de Extranjería must resolve the residence authorization within 1 month of receiving the consulate's communication; silence = refusal (Hoja 6). Once granted, the applicant has 1 month to collect the visa. Real-world times vary by consulate and BLS appointment availability; no official average published.

fees.label: National visa fee (US citizens, reciprocity rate)
fees.note: Chicago page lists 2026: Americans $140, other nationalities $106. Houston and Boston also state $140 for US passport holders. Washington says rates apply by reciprocity and are revised quarterly with exchange rates. Paid by money order; non-refundable. BLS service charges are extra and not included.

fees.label: Residence authorization fee (Modelo 790 código 052, epígrafe 2.1.1)
fees.note: Chicago: fee for 2026 is $13 (also $13 at Boston, Houston, Washington). Per applicant. Total per applicant at the consulate: $140 + $13 = $153. TIE card fee in Spain is separate and not verified here.

duration.renewal: Renewable for 2 years at a time, then eligible for long-term residence after 5 years
duration.note: Initial authorization lasts 1 year from entry (Hoja 6). Visa itself valid up to 90 days for entry (Boston; Hoja 6: never more than 3 months). Renewed authorization valid 2 years unless long-term residence applies (Hoja 7); apply in the 2 months before expiry or up to 3 months after. Renewal also requires sufficient means for the renewal period.

workAllowed.note: Boston: the visa 'does not allow any type of work or professional activity, including remote, as this is not a digital nomad visa.' Hoja 6: authorizes residence without carrying out work or professional activities.

pathToPR.note: Residencia de larga duración (national): 5 years of legal and continuous residence in Spain before applying (Hoja 49; Ley Orgánica 4/2000 art. 32; RD 1155/2024). Long-term EU status (Hoja 50) also requires 5 years. Absence limits that break continuity are not verified here.

pathToCitizenship.note: Código Civil art. 22.1 (as amended by Ley 36/2002): naturalization by residence requires 10 years of legal, continuous residence immediately before applying. The 2-year reduced period applies only to nationals of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal and Sephardic Jews; US citizens are not covered. Art. 23 requires renouncing prior nationality (US not exempt). Resolution time: max 1 year, silence = refusal (Ley 36/2002 DA).

steps.title: Gather documents in the US
steps.detail: EX-01 form, passport valid 1+ year, FBI fingerprint background check (max 6 months old) with FBI Apostille and sworn Spanish translation, medical certificate (max 3 months old), proof of means (400% IPREM), Spanish health insurance with no copay or limits, proof of residence in the consular district.

steps.title: Apply in person at the consulate (or its BLS centre) for your US state
steps.detail: Each US consulate only accepts residents of its district. Pay the $140 visa fee + $13 Modelo 790-052 fee per applicant.

steps.title: Wait for the decision (legal limit 3 months)
steps.detail: The consulate forwards the file to the Spanish immigration office, which resolves the residence authorization within 1 month of receiving it.

steps.title: Collect the visa within 1 month and enter Spain within its validity
steps.detail: Visa valid for up to 3 months; the 1-year authorization starts on the date of entry.

steps.title: Apply for the TIE (foreigner ID card) within 1 month of entry
steps.detail: In person at the Policía Nacional station or Oficina de Extranjería for your place of residence.

steps.title: Renew before the first year ends
steps.detail: Apply in the 2 months before expiry; renewal gives 2 more years if means are maintained.

visas.verificationNotes: Changes vs app: fee was ~EUR 600, verified US-citizen fee is $140 visa + $13 residence fee = $153 per applicant (2026, Chicago/Houston/Boston). Processing: app said 2-3 months; official legal maximum is 3 months (no official minimum). Income unchanged at EUR 2,400/mo (IPREM still EUR 600 in 2026 because the 2023 budget is prorogued). Not verified: TIE card fee, BLS service charges, exact absence limits for PR/citizenship continuity, whether every US consulate charges the same $140 (Washington page only says 'reciprocity rates, revised quarterly'). RD 1155/2024 (in force May 2025) now governs NLV (arts. 60-63); the official Hoja 6 updated May 2025 keeps 400%/100% IPREM and 1-year initial term; renewal sheet (Hoja 7) states 2-year renewals. Some secondary sources claim the new reglamento lets NLV holders switch to work authorizations; not verified from an official page, so not included.

visas.name: Digital Nomad Visa (visado para teletrabajo de carácter internacional, Ley 14/2013 as amended by Ley 28/2022)

income.basis: 200% of the monthly SMI (SMI 2026 = EUR 1,221/month in 14 payments, EUR 17,094/year; Real Decreto 126/2026)
income.perDependent: First family member +75% SMI (EUR 916/month); each additional member +25% SMI (EUR 305/month)
income.note: Rule from the joint DGM/DGEEAC instruction of 29 Mar 2023 (https://www.inclusion.gob.es/documents/410169/0/report_report_2301+Instrucci%C3%B3n+conjunta+Teletrabajadores+de+car%C3%A1cter+internacional_rev13_FIRMADAS.pdf/d6c8533a-c98e-6157-da03-a598f0e1c017?t=1681813834808): holder 200% SMI monthly; 2-person family unit +75% SMI; +25% SMI per additional member. SMI 2026 = EUR 40.70/day or EUR 1,221/month (RD 126/2026, BOE-A-2026-3815, https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/2026/02/18/126/con), EUR 17,094/year (SEPE). Houston consulate (official) computes on the monthly figure: 2 x 1,221 = 2,442/month (~$2,845); 0.75 x 1,221 = 915.75 ~ 916; 0.25 x 1,221 = 305.25 ~ 305. CONFLICT: many secondary sources prorate the 14-payment annual SMI over 12 months: 17,094 / 12 = 1,424.50; x 2 = 2,849/month (34,188/year); family +1,068.38 and +356.13. Ministry of Inclusión (UGE) historically used the prorated figure for in-Spain residence applications (2025: EUR 2,762 = 16,576 x 2 / 12), but no official 2026 UGE page confirming 2,849 was found. Annual left null because the official consular page gives only a monthly figure. Safe planning figure: EUR 2,849/month. Couple (Houston basis): 2,442 + 916 = 3,358/month; couple + 1 child: 3,663/month.

savings.note: No separate savings threshold on US consulate pages; requirement is expressed as monthly income (any means of proof: employment contract, firm job offer, commercial contract). Some non-US consulates mention 'own financial means' as an alternative; not verified for US consulates.

processingTimeDays.note: Value is in BUSINESS days (días hábiles), about 2 calendar weeks. Ley 14/2013 art. 75.5: visa applications are resolved and notified within 10 business days (Houston consulate repeats this; extendable if an interview or extra documents are needed). In-Spain residence authorization via UGE (art. 76.1): max 20 days from electronic filing, positive silence (approved if no answer). Real-world consular times and BLS appointment waits vary; not officially published.

fees.label: National visa fee (US citizens, reciprocity rate)
fees.note: Houston page: 'Americans $190'. Miami page (https://www.exteriores.gob.es/Consulados/miami/en/ServiciosConsulares/Paginas/TELEWORK-VISA.aspx) states Americans $190, other nationalities $94, 'from Jan. 1st 2025' (not updated label for 2026). New York 2025 fee list: visas under the Law of Entrepreneurs $190. Money order; non-refundable. NIE fee, BLS charges and the in-Spain UGE residence fee not verified here.

duration.renewal: Visa holders can apply in Spain for a residence authorization of up to 3 years (within 60 days before visa expiry); renewals for 2 years each
duration.note: Ley 14/2013 art. 74 quater: visa valid max 1 year (or shorter if the work period is shorter); art. 74 quater.3: residence application in the 60 natural days before visa expiry; art. 74 quinquies.2: residence authorization max 3 years; art. 76.3: renewals for 2-year periods. Applicants already legally in Spain can apply directly to the UGE for the 3-year residence without a visa.

workAllowed.note: Ley 14/2013 art. 74 bis.1: employees may only work for companies located outside Spain; self-employed may work for Spanish companies up to 20% of their total professional activity. Work must be remote via telematic means. Requires 3+ months' relationship with the foreign employer/clients and the company must have operated at least 1 year (art. 74 ter).

pathToPR.note: Residencia de larga duración: 5 years of legal and continuous residence (Hoja 49; Ley Orgánica 4/2000 art. 32). Time on the DNV counts as legal residence (inference: it is a residence title under Ley 14/2013; no official page found that addresses DNV time explicitly).

pathToCitizenship.note: Código Civil art. 22.1: 10 years of legal, continuous residence; US citizens do not qualify for the 2-year reduced period (Ibero-America, Andorra, Philippines, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal, Sephardic). Art. 23: renunciation of prior nationality required.

steps.title: Get a Spanish NIE number from your consulate
steps.detail: Houston and other US consulates require the NIE before the visa application.

steps.title: Gather documents
steps.detail: Employer/client certificate (3+ months, remote work allowed), company active 1+ year, degree or 3 years' experience, income 200% SMI, FBI background check with Apostille and translation, health insurance, and US Social Security Certificate of Coverage (US-Spain agreement) or Spanish Social Security registration.

steps.title: Apply in person at your consulate's BLS centre and pay $190
steps.detail: Only residents of the consular district may apply there.

steps.title: Decision within 10 business days
steps.detail: Legal deadline under Ley 14/2013 art. 75.5; longer if an interview or more documents are requested.

steps.title: Move to Spain; the 1-year visa is your residence title
steps.detail: A TIE card is optional during the visa year and can be requested at the Oficina de Extranjería or Police station.

steps.title: Apply to the UGE for the 3-year residence authorization
steps.detail: File online within the 60 days before the visa expires; UGE must answer within 20 days (silence = approval).

steps.title: Get your TIE
steps.detail: Authorizations valid over 6 months require applying for the foreigner identity card (Ley 14/2013 art. 76.2).

visas.verificationNotes: INCOME CONFLICT: official Houston consulate page = EUR 2,442/month (2 x 1,221 monthly SMI); widely cited secondary figure = EUR 2,849/month (17,094 x 2 / 12, prorated). No official 2026 UGE or Ministry page found stating 2,849; one secondary report (GPA, May 2026) even claims the Ministry kept EUR 2,762. Treat EUR 2,849 as the conservative planning figure. Dependents: official rule is +75% SMI for the first family member and +25% per additional member (not specifically 'spouse' and 'child'). Processing: app said 20-45 days; statutory maximum is 10 business days for the consular visa and 20 days for UGE residence. Fee: app value not given for DNV; US citizens pay $190 (Houston, Miami; Miami label says 'from Jan 1 2025'). Washington page fee table not machine-readable. Not verified: NIE fee, BLS service charge, UGE residence fee, TIE fee, whether DNV time counts toward PR explicitly. RD 1155/2024 (in force May 2025) is the general immigration reglamento; the DNV is governed by Ley 14/2013 and the 2023 joint instruction, and no official source found indicating the new reglamento changed DNV thresholds or durations (inference).
